title: Demonstration of subspace-search variational quantum eigensolver using photonic orbital angular momentum qudits
authors: Kang-Min Hu, Myung-Hyun Sohn, Yong-Su Kim, Kwang Jo Lee, Hyun Woo Kim, Hyang-Tag Lim
abstract: Accurate excited state energies are essential for interpreting fluorescence and photochemical processes, yet variational quantum eigensolvers (VQEs) on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware have largely been confined to ground states. Subspace-search VQE (SSVQE) offers a NISQ-friendly route to excited states without ancilla-based overlap measurements, however it has lacked an experimental demonstration since it requires the coherent preparation and manipulation of multiple orthogonal basis states under a shared variational unitary. Here we realize SSVQE on a photonic platform by encoding orthogonal qudit states in the orbital angular momentum of single photons and optimizing a shared variational circuit. We estimate excited state energies for a four-dimensional $\rm{HeH^+}$ molecule and an eight-dimensional Heisenberg chain, thereby demonstrating scalable excited state eigensolving in a high-dimensional Hilbert space. Our results establish photonic qudits as a resource-efficient pathway to excited state quantum simulation.
summary: This paper demonstrates the use of Subspace-search VQE (SSVQE) to calculate excited state energies using photons whose quantum states are encoded in orbital angular momentum (OAM) qudits. By implementing this on a photonic platform, the authors show a scalable and resource-efficient method for simulating complex molecular and quantum chain Hamiltonians beyond ground state calculations.
main_problem: Accurately estimating excited state energies is crucial for interpreting photochemical processes, but variational quantum eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically limited to ground states.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated Subspace-search VQE (SSVQE) on a photonic platform, estimating excited state energies for molecular and quantum chain systems.
method: They use SSVQE, a NISQ-friendly approach, by encoding quantum information in the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of single photons to estimate multiple eigenenergies simultaneously.
model_or_system: The experiment is performed on a photonic platform using single photons whose quantum states are encoded in OAM qudits. They apply this method to model a four-dimensional HeH+ molecule and an eight-dimensional Heisenberg chain.
key_observables: Estimated excited state energies ($\langle E_j angle$) for the target Hamiltonians, and the convergence of these energies over optimization iterations.
important_parameters: The variational parameters ($\vec{\alpha}$) controlling the shared variational unitary circuit, and the dimension of the Hilbert space ($d=4$ or $d=8$).
main_assumptions: The method avoids ancilla-based overlap measurements, relying instead on the coherent preparation and measurement of orthogonal OAM qudit states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the iterative SSVQE cycle between the QPU, CPU, and classical optimizer. Figure 2 shows the experimental setup using SLMs for state preparation and measurement. Figures 3 and 4 show the calculated energy spectra for HeH+ and the Heisenberg chain, respectively.
paper_structure: The paper details the SSVQE algorithm, describes the photonic implementation using OAM qudits and SLMs, presents the experimental setup, and finally reports the successful estimation of excited state energies for the molecular and chain models.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the challenge of excited state simulation in quantum chemistry using photonic hardware, establishing a resource-efficient pathway for high-dimensional quantum simulation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. OAM qudit–based SSVQE procedure. At it- eration n, a set of N mutually orthogonal variational states {|ψj(⃗αn)⟩}N−1 j=0 is prepared by displaying the corresponding holograms on a SLM. Each state is measured on the photonic QPU (quantum processing unit) using a set of Pauli-string observables (implemented with a second SLM), from which the Hamiltonian expectation values are estimated. The CPU (classical processing unit) evaluates the SSVQE cost function L and a classical optimizer (COBYLA) updates the param- eters ⃗αn+1 to minimize L. The procedure is repeated until convergence, |∆n| = |⃗αn+1 −⃗αn| < ϵ, yielding the optimized energies ⟨E0⟩min, ⟨E1⟩min, . . . , ⟨EN−1⟩min...

FIG. 2. Experimental setup for SSVQE. Photon pairs are generated via type-II SPDC; the idler photon is detected by APD1 to herald the signal photon, which is sent to the QPU for SSVQE. In the QPU, the signal photon is prepared in the jth OAM ansatz qudit state |ψj(⃗αn)⟩by displaying the corresponding hologram on SLM1. The diffracted beam is spatially filtered (iris) and analyzed using measurement holograms on SLM2 to perform Pauli-string measurements. The measurement outcomes are processed by the CPU to evaluate the cost function L and update the variational parameters ⃗α via a classical optimizer.
